title: Rate limits & Org/Project Keys demo with Crestwood Health
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a demo focused on org/project API keys, per-project rate limits, quota policies, and how the console surfaces usage and alerts. Customer (Crestwood Health) has multi-tenant product with strict tenant isolation requirements and enterprise security controls; main asks: per-tenant quotas, easy key rotation, SAML integration, SOC2 artifacts, and predictable behavior under burst traffic. Agreed next steps: send security pack and pricing, provide trial project keys for a 2-week POC, schedule dedicated latency benchmark with SEs.
next_steps: Alex to share SOC2 + security pack (by 2026-04-07)
Priya to provision trial org/project keys and sample policies (by 2026-04-02)
Schedule POC benchmark: 1-hour run with Crestwood traffic profile (tentative week of 2026-04-13)
action_items: Owner: Alex Morgan | Item: Share security docs (SOC2 report, ISO certs, whitepaper) | Due: 2026-04-07
Owner: Priya Shah | Item: Create trial org with two project keys + example rate limit policies | Due: 2026-04-02
Owner: Dana Li | Item: Share expected QPS, percentiles for seq lengths & busiest endpoints | Due: 2026-04-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dana Li (Crestwood CTO), Mark Reyes (Eng Manager), Saira Khan (Security Architect)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Demo of org/project keys and rate limiting, console walkthrough, discussed security & POC next steps.

00:00 Alex: okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, uh priya from our se team will do the walkthrough, thanks for the time
00:12 Dana: yeah thanks alex, excited to see how you do per-tenant limits — we have a multi-tenant product so that is the big thing for us
00:20 Alex: great, quick agenda: 1) high level org vs project keys 2) console demo of quotas & alerts 3) API examples and behavior on 429s 4) Q&A and next steps
00:38 Priya: i'll share my screen in a sec — just to call out: we built org/project keys so you can centralize billing per org while issuing project-scoped keys to tenants, and then apply both global and per-project quotas
00:56 Mark: cool, so project keys are what we'd give each tenant in prod, and org keys are for internal services?
01:03 Priya: exactly, org keys are for admin/backoffice or cross-tenant jobs, project keys are scoped down, they also support RBAC, and you can rotate independently
01:20 Saira: security question — do project keys live in our VPC for private deploys or are they managed by redwood?
01:27 Alex: good question — in hosted, keys are managed by redwood but you can require customer-managed KMS for certain tokens; for private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and keys never leave your control
01:38 Dana: okay thanks, that helps. can you show the console?
01:45 Priya: yep sharing, ok you should see the org dashboard, top left — usage overview, token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency and errors
02:10 Priya: here's a list of projects under Crestwood-Prod; each project row shows a current QPS, daily quota, and status. you can click into project to set a rate limit policy — e.g., 200 qps sustained, 500 burst with leaky-bucket smoothing
02:35 Mark: what's the enforcement model? are limits applied at the gateway or upstream?
02:40 Priya: enforcement is at the edge on our serving fleet — we use a token-bucket style limiter per project key plus a global org fallback; that lets you protect noisy tenants while still allowing short bursts
02:56 Priya: also you can combine per-route quotas — so if you want to limit embeddings differently than generation or streaming endpoints, you can set route-level caps
03:14 Saira: how does billing work when we have per-project quotas? do you get charged per org and then re-bill tenants?
03:20 Alex: for hosted customers we meter per-token per-project so you get detailed breakdown; billing can be at org level, and you can export per-project usage for internal chargeback
03:32 Dana: what about overage? if someone exceeds quota will requests 429 or be queued?
03:38 Priya: default is 429 with Retry-After header; we also offer a throttling policy that softly degrades — e.g., lower model quality or route to cheaper variant — but that's a paid policy and configurable per org
03:54 Mark: do you provide webhooks or alerts when a project approaches limit?
03:58 Priya: yep, threshold alerts can be set — you get console notifications, email, and we can post to slack or webhook. plus long-term spikes are surfaced in the Optimize tab
04:18 Dana: curious about keys — rotation and audit logs. we need key rotation every quarter and full audit trails for compliance
04:26 Alex: rotation is supported via the console or API, you can create a new project key and do live rollover; we keep immutable audit logs with who-rotated, when, and the context (for private deployment logs can be sent to your SIEM)
04:42 Saira: do logs contain PII or payloads? we can't have full payloads forwarded externally
04:47 Priya: by default logs are metadata only (request id, model, latency, tokens). full payload logging is optional and can be disabled; for private we can route logs to your storage and redact payloads at ingestion
05:05 Alex: moving to API examples — priya, can you show a curl for project key usage and how rate limit headers look?
05:11 Priya: sure, here's a sample curl: Authorization: Bearer <PROJECT_KEY> to the v1/generate endpoint. headers we return: x-rw-rate-limit-limit, x-rw-rate-limit-remaining, x-rw-rate-limit-reset, and on 429 we include Retry-After and a link to quota object id in body
05:36 Mark: are those headers per-route or aggregated?
05:40 Priya: per-route + per-project. so you'll see route-level bucket and an org-level bucket; the client can reconcile and backoff accordingly
05:52 Dana: do you support client libraries that automatically backoff?
05:56 Alex: our SDKs include a built-in retry/backoff policy with jitter, exponential backoff, and optional sticky token-bucket behavior so you don't thundering-herd at the gateway
06:10 Priya: i'll simulate a burst — toggling a synthetic traffic generator in the console. you'll see we hit the project bucket first then org fallback kicks in
06:20 [30s silence while demo runs, faint keyboard sounds]
06:52 Priya: okay, you'll see a climb in the QPS graph and then a flatten where rate limiter started returning 429 for the offending project; the project remained healthy overall due to org fallback for some critical routes
07:12 Mark: that looks promising. do you offer warm/cold token cache hints for latency sensitive paths?
07:18 Priya: we do prefix caching plus KV cache for generation state; that helps latency for repeated prompts or session chats. cache is per-instance but synced with our routing to prefer warm instances for active sessions
07:36 Saira: in our security review we need SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the console
07:42 Alex: yes SAML SSO, SCIM, fine-grained RBAC are available for enterprise plans; we also support org-level admin roles and project-specific roles
07:55 Dana: for POC we want to simulate our busiest tenant — we'll need a trial project key that mirrors their QPS and token distribution
08:03 Priya: absolutely we can provision two project keys that mirror your tenant profile and a small test org to run. i'll also include a pre-built workload script to replay traffic patterns
08:18 Dana: can you support private deployment for regulatory data residency? some of our tenants are in EU and require data to remain in EU region only
08:26 Alex: yes — we have private deployment options. for hosted we can pin region-specific serving and data residency controls; for regulated workloads we recommend private with your VPC and customer-managed KMS
08:40 Saira: any compliance artifacts you can share now?
08:44 Alex: i'll send the SOC2Type2, ISO27001 summary, and our data processing addendum — you'll get them in the security pack after the call
08:55 Mark: ok thanks. quick question on quotas per customer tier: can we have different quotas for free vs paid tenants?
09:02 Priya: yep, you can create policy templates and apply them to a project or label-based selector — e.g., plan=free -> 10 qps, plan=pro -> 200 qps. templates can be inherited at org or project level
09:18 Dana: and are these editable via API? we want infra-as-code changes
09:22 Priya: everything in the console is backed by an API, so you can manage policies via terraform or our REST API. we also have webhooks for policy change events
09:36 Mark: what's the delay for policy changes to propagate?
09:40 Priya: typical propagation under 10s for rate limit rules; for larger deployment topology changes it can be a minute or two but not more than 120s in our tests
09:55 Saira: do you have RBAC on who can change quotas? we must prevent product managers from easing limits accidentally
09:59 Alex: yes, role based permissions — you can restrict quota edits to admins only; changes are logged and require approval workflow if you subscribe to the enterprise workflow addon
10:12 Dana: let's talk edge cases: if a tenant hits quota during a batch job that runs overnight, can we allow queueing or reserved burst for scheduled jobs?
10:23 Priya: you can create reservation windows or scheduled burst allowances — e.g., reserve 10k tokens between 2am-4am for a specific project; the scheduler honors reservations before general bucket consumption
10:38 Mark: how do you handle backpressure for streaming responses? we can't drop open sockets easily
10:43 Priya: streaming responses use a separate token accounting path and we offer graceful degradation: either continue with smaller chunk sizes or complete with an abbreviated response; the stream connection stays open and you receive a partial but well formed result
10:59 Dana: curious about multi-tenant isolation at the hardware level — do noisy neighbors ever impact latency?
11:06 Alex: in hosted we isolate with per-project scheduling and autoscaling; we also offer Dedicated pools where you get reserved GPU capacity for an org to avoid noisy neighbor entirely
11:18 Priya: dedicated pools are common for customers with tight p99 SLOs; Dedicated also gives you isolated metrics and separate billing/reporting
11:30 Dana: for our initial POC, we want hosted with project keys but potentially move to dedicated if p99 latency is poor
11:36 Alex: that's a common path — start hosted to iterate quickly then reserve Dedicated capacity when pattern stabilizes. we can also do a hybrid where mission-critical routes hit dedicated and others hit hosted
11:50 Mark: any rate limiting algorithm options? token bucket vs leaky bucket vs adaptive?
11:56 Priya: we support token-bucket by default, leaky-bucket smoothing, and an adaptive controller that uses recent latency signals to throttle dynamically; adaptive is opt-in and recommended for bursty traffic
12:14 Dana: what's the expected behavior for long-running requests that exceed token allocation mid-request? do you fail mid-stream?
12:21 Priya: we attempt graceful completion; if mid-request you exceed account limits we can either finish the current request (billing applies) or cut off based on your policy. default is allow finish for started requests unless you opt into strict enforcement
12:40 Saira: does finishing incur the same quota? want to avoid a single long job draining everyone's quota unexpectedly
12:46 Alex: you can mark routes as "billing-exempt" or set request caps; also, reservation windows can protect critical services from being drained by large one-offs
12:58 Mark: how do you surface which tenant caused a spike, like forensic info?
13:04 Priya: the analytics tab ties request ids to project keys and shows a per-project breakdown with sample request metadata (no payloads unless enabled), plus a heatmap of top-token consumers across time
13:22 Dana: anything else on security? we also need SSO audit logs and SCIM provisioning timestamps
13:28 Alex: covered — audit logs for console actions, key rotations, policy changes, and SCIM provisioning events are retained per your retention policy and exportable to your SIEM
13:40 Priya: i'm going to demo how to create a project key and set a quota template now
13:44 [screen share click, console navigation noises]
14:02 Priya: create project -> name "tenant-demo" -> create key -> copy ; now in policies -> create template -> name "pro-tier" -> qps 200, burst 500, daily token cap 5M -> apply to project tenant-demo
14:26 Mark: can we set different quotas per model family e.g., embeddings vs chat?
14:31 Priya: yes, route selectors let you pick endpoints like /embeddings, /chat or model tags like gpt-open-embedding; you can apply different caps and overage behaviors
14:50 Dana: can the console export a sample policy to JSON so we can check into git?
14:54 Priya: yes, export policy -> JSON, we also have a terraform provider that mirrors the same objects
15:06 Mark: ok good. about the trial keys — will they have the same rate limiting behavior as production? we need fidelity
15:12 Priya: trial keys are provisioned in a test org that mimics production limits; we can provision them with the same policies as production so your benchmark is realistic
15:25 Dana: we'll need a dedicated test for priority routes — message routing and streaming p99 are most important
15:30 Priya: noted. we'll include a benchmark script that records p50/p95/p99 and token costs so you can compare. SE will help run the test with you
15:44 Alex: on pricing, i'll include a reference sheet — hosted per-token pricing, plus a Dedicated reserve quote if you choose that route. i can also include an example of cost breakdown for your tenant mix
15:58 Saira: any contractual SLAs for rate limiting? if redwood throttles us incorrectly we need recourse
16:06 Alex: enterprise contracts include SLA language for uptime and latency targets, plus credits for violations; we can add a clause for guaranteed policy propagation times for high-tier customers
16:20 Mark: let's capture one more complex scenario: org-wide auto-throttle that reduces model size when under load to keep latency. is that automatic?
16:28 Priya: we have a fallback policy that routes to smaller/quantized model variants when thresholds are hit; it's configurable per route and can be set to automatic or manual failover
16:42 Dana: does that change token cost math? smaller models usually cost less but may produce different quality — we need quality monitoring
16:49 Alex: Optimize provides quality monitoring and regression alerts against your eval sets — you can tie a prompt set to a route and alert if output drift exceeds threshold when falling back to cheaper models
17:05 Mark: what about ML evals integrated into the pipeline? can we run periodic regressions when policies change?
17:12 Priya: yes, we support scheduled eval runs and will surface quality deltas; Optimize can gate rollouts if quality drops below threshold
17:28 Dana: great. really helpful demo. a few administrative notes: we'll need the SOC2 doc, proposed pricing, trial keys, and a POC benchmark scheduled
17:38 Alex: yep will send the pack. priya will provision keys. dana, mark, anything else?
17:44 Mark: maybe a short follow-up to review benchmark results, 30 min sync after the run
17:49 Dana: agreed
17:52 Saira: one more question: can we rotate keys programmatically on schedule? we prefer automation
17:56 Priya: yes we have rotation API and you can set rotation cadence; we also support short-lived keys issued by your STS for ephemeral workloads
18:10 Alex: perfect. i'll recap in email and add calendar invites for the benchmark and follow-up
18:16 [wrap-up small talk]
18:30 Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with security pack and keys. bye

End of transcript
